top_story: Israeli leaders are moving from coercive rhetoric toward a more structured depopulation agenda for Gaza: after the defence minister reiterated on 2 September that Israel still seeks to remove Palestinians from the territory, he pushed for Donald Trump’s backing for expulsion, and by 3 September Itamar Ben Gvir was preparing to tie a $20 billion seven-year removal plan to future coalition negotiations. This sequence suggests forced transfer is being normalized across Israel’s right rather than floated as an isolated provocation, deepening existential pressure on Gaza’s surviving population and hardening regional perceptions that war aims now extend beyond military defeat to demographic engineering. In parallel, Iran’s 3 September strikes on US bases in Kuwait, launched despite Trump’s threats and after US raids earlier in the week, widen the confrontation into the Gulf and sharpen the sense that Washington’s regional posture is feeding simultaneous escalation tracks. The combined effect is a more combustible regional environment in which mass displacement in Gaza and direct US-Iran confrontation increasingly reinforce each other’s political logic.
